messages:
alicia: Heads-up — noticed steady KV cache memory growth on host m-12 during longctx runs. Graphs show per-tenant residency for t-42 keeps rising even after requests stop. Anyone else see this pattern?

mike: yup saw similar on m-7 yesterday. suspect reuse windows not getting compacted for tenants that do intermittent longctx.

zach: @alicia can you paste the pprof heap diff? curious whether it's live slices or fragmented slabs.

alicia: quick snippet from heap diff:```
# heap profile: 48MB -> 96MB
6000 bytes  8.7%  8.7%  runtime.mSpanNew  <...>
42000 bytes 76.5% 85.2% github.com/redwood/runtime/kv.(*Page).cacheEntry
```

carla: that cacheEntry domination suggests page headers / meta are sticking around. maybe our tenant lease window leaves them pinned.

mike: also saw high fragmentation in pmap at the same time — free list isn't coalescing because sizes vary.

alicia: hypothesis: when a tenant with longctx bursts, we create many small suffix pages; our eviction prefers whole-page LRU so fragments survive. Result: other tenants see reduced effective residency.

zach: sounds like noisy-neighbor. current per-tenant quota is a soft watermark (credits decaying over 15m). Could tighten to a token-bucket with hard cap + reclaim priority.

carla: proposal: 1) add forced compaction pass after idle window (2m) to merge small free slabs. 2) change quota to two-tier: soft burst + hard steady. 3) instrument per-tenant fragmentation metric.

mike: +1. We should be careful about perf regressions from compaction. Maybe run compaction as low-priority background task gated by GPU utilization < 30%.

alicia: agreed. I'll sketch an experiment: switch t-42 to hard cap 256MB, run compaction background at low-prio, collect latency and p99 token timings for 30m. Anyone want to own the instrumentation dash?

zach: I can add per-tenant frag% and resident_pages histogram to console. ETA: end of day.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: kv-compact-experiment -> staging at 2026-03-18T16:40Z :rocket:

carla: for the experiment, add an annotation with the tenant label and exact workload (longctx-qa). We'll need baseline traces for comparison.

alicia: noted. I'll capture baseline traces now and post link. Thanks all :thumbsup:
